featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited PVR Icon at Phoenix Palladium Mall, Lower Parel to watch the intense and gripping film *Tere Ishq Mein*, and the overall experience turned out to be truly awesome. From the moment we entered, the theatre carried a premium feel that perfectly matched the high-octane mood of the movie. The cleanliness was impressive, with spotless floors, fresh seats, and a well-maintained auditorium that immediately made us comfortable.

The atmosphere was classy and inviting, exactly what one expects from an ICON-format cinema. The lighting, décor, and overall layout added a modern, upscale touch to the outing. The sound quality was excellent, enhancing every emotional beat and intense moment of Tere Ishq Mein, Dialogues were crisp, background score was immersive, and the action-heavy scenes carried real impact. The seats were comfortable, spacious, and well-cushioned, allowing us to enjoy the long movie without any discomfort.

What added to the joy was that it was a perfect Sunday outing. After the movie, we explored Phoenix Palladium — always lively, beautifully maintained, and full of great options for shopping and food. Being from North India, we naturally gravitated to Punjab Grill for lunch, and it turned out to be a wonderful choice. The food was rich, flavourful, and truly reminded us of home. The combination of delicious North Indian dishes and the mall’s vibrant ambience made the outing even more memorable.

In short, our visit to PVR Icon at Phoenix Palladium was a fantastic experience. The movie was intense, the theatre offered top-notch comfort and quality, and the day ended perfectly with a satisfying meal and a relaxed stroll through the mall. A Sunday well spent.

featured_reviews.name: Ganesh Rajak
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing experience at PVR Phoenix Palladium Mall! The luxurious Recliner seats, crystal-clear clean quality, and immersive sound system made the movie experience absolutely premium. One of the Best theatres in Mumbai !! ✨

featured_reviews.name: Veikho Asanii
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a change of pace and to explore something new, I caught a late-night movie at the PVR ICON (with Dolby Atmos) in Phoenix Palladium Mall, Lower Parel. It was a fantastic deal!
From the spacious lobby to the neat and well-maintained theatre, this place really stands out compared to other PVR locations I've visited. They offer a great variety of food items and excellent coffee options.
The seating—from sofa-style loungers to premium theatre seats—felt more like luxury, and in some ways, it was even better than the Gold Class Premier screens at other PVRs.
One standout observation: the sound engineer must be incredibly skillful. This delivered the best audio experience I've ever had in a PVR theatre—the Dolby Atmos immersion was top-notch!
Highly recommended place for anyone looking for a premium movie outing. Definitely worth it!

I recently visited Metro INOX Cinema, and my overall experience was extremely enjoyable and comfortable. This cinema hall perfectly blends a classic feel with modern movie-watching amenities, making it a great choice for both regular viewers and cinema lovers who appreciate a well-maintained theatre.

The screen and sound quality were excellent. The visuals were sharp, bright, and immersive, which made the movie even more engaging. The sound system was well balanced—loud enough to create impact without being overwhelming. Dialogues were clear, and background music and effects were crisp, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.

The seating arrangement deserves special mention. The seats were comfortable, well-spaced, and offered a clear view of the screen from almost every angle. Legroom was sufficient, allowing for a relaxed experience even during a long movie. The auditorium was clean and well maintained, which added to the comfort level.

The ambience of Metro INOX has a pleasant and premium feel. The lobby area was neat, organized, and not overly crowded. The lighting and interiors give a classy vibe, making the wait time before the show quite comfortable. Entry and exit were well managed, avoiding unnecessary rush or confusion.

Food and beverages were also satisfactory. The snacks counter offered the usual cinema favourites like popcorn, cold drinks, and nachos. While prices are on the higher side—as expected in multiplexes—the quality and freshness were good. The staff at the counter were polite and quick in handling orders, even during peak hours.

Another positive aspect was the staff behavior and overall management. The staff members were helpful, courteous, and ensured smooth operations throughout the show. Ticket checking, seating guidance, and cleanliness were handled efficiently. Restrooms were clean and well maintained, which is an important factor for any public place.

Overall, Metro INOX Cinema provides a reliable, comfortable, and enjoyable movie-watching experience. Whether you’re going for a weekend show with friends, a family outing, or a solo movie break, this place delivers on quality, comfort, and ambience. I would definitely recommend Metro INOX Cinema to anyone looking for a pleasant and hassle-free cinema experience.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The National Museum of Indian Cinema is a really interesting place for anyone who loves movies or wants to know how Indian cinema has changed over the years. The museum has old film cameras, posters, movie costumes, and many interactive sections that make the experience fun instead of boring.
The place is divided into two buildings Gulshan Mahal and a modern glass building. Every floor has something different to see, like the history of Indian cinema, famous actors and directors, music, filmmaking, and behind the scenes information. I also liked seeing sections dedicated to legends like Dadasaheb Phalke, Satyajit Ray, and Raj Kapoor. The museum is clean, well maintained, and not too crowded, so you can explore peacefully at your own pace. Some sections feel nostalgic, especially if you grew up watching Bollywood movies.
Overall, it’s a unique place in Mumbai and worth visiting once. Keep at least 2-3 hours because there’s a lot to explore inside.

They also offer a headphone which explains the history of the different stages of Indian cinema through time.
A must visit place for the ones who love cinema and movies.

featured_reviews.name: Athen
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a big fan of cinema this museum was a must visit for me. It is an excellent place for people who love art, history, storytelling or cinema. This museum does an excellent job of capturing the evolution of India cinema from it's inception till date.

The museum is divided into two buildings, the first one being a showcase of India cinema as a whole and the second one is a four story building where you start from the top floor and keep descending. Each floor has something unique to show about a particular aspect of movies. There are a lot of interactive displays that only enhance the experience.

The place is clean, calm and not crowded at all making it an ideal experience. 1-2 hours are enough to go around the whole place. The tickets used to be free for children and students but now they've changed that and everyone is charged 165 Rs for the ticket.

Overall, it’s a well-curated, informative, and enjoyable museum that truly celebrates the legacy of Indian cinema. Highly recommended for students, filmmakers, and casual visitors alike.

featured_reviews.name: Naihrit Halder
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Eros IMAX, Mumbai, and it ended up being one of my favourite movie experiences in the city. There’s something special about this place—the moment you see the iconic art‑deco building from outside, it already feels different from the typical multiplex vibe.
Inside, the theatre is spacious, clean, and surprisingly comfortable. The IMAX screen here genuinely enhances the movie experience without overwhelming you, and the sound quality is crystal clear. I watched a film here recently, and the visuals + audio made it feel so immersive.
One thing I really appreciate about Eros is how well-organized everything is—from the ticket counters to entering the auditorium. The staff was polite and helpful, and the crowd felt more relaxed compared to the usual rush you see in other cinemas.
Snacks are priced reasonably for a theatre in South Mumbai, and the washrooms and waiting areas are clean and well-maintained.
Plus, walking out after the show into the Churchgate/Marine Drive area just completes the whole experience. It’s one of the few cinemas where both the movie and the location feel equally enjoyable.
Definitely a great spot for movie lovers. I’d happily visit again!

featured_reviews.name: ARYAN PATIL
featured_reviews.review_text: Watched a movie at Eros INOX and had a great experience overall. The screen quality is excellent with sharp visuals, and the sound system is immersive, making the movie truly engaging. Seating is comfortable with good legroom, so even long movies feel relaxed. The theatre is clean, well maintained, and the staff is organized, which makes entry and exit smooth. Definitely one of the better places in the city to enjoy a movie.

featured_reviews.name: Arjun Pitroda
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an incredible experience at Eros INOX! I’ve watched two IMAX movies here recently and both were spectacular. The restoration is stunning—they’ve kept the classic Art Deco charm and those iconic marble stairs, but the theater itself is world-class. The IMAX with Laser technology is super sharp, and the sound is immersive without being overwhelming. It’s easily one of the best places in Mumbai to catch a blockbuster. Highly recommend for the nostalgia and the tech!

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Stunning Revival of a Mumbai Icon!

I recently visited the newly revamped Eros Theatre at Churchgate, now under the PVR banner and featuring a grand IMAX screen. I must say, the experience was nothing short of spectacular.

The restoration has beautifully retained the Art Deco charm of this iconic building, blending heritage with modern technology seamlessly. From the moment you enter, the space exudes elegance and nostalgia, yet feels fresh and world-class.

The IMAX screen is massive and immersive, and the sound system is crystal clear, delivering every note and dialogue with incredible depth. Seats are comfortable, the ambience is premium, and the entire setup does justice to both classic cinema lovers and modern moviegoers.

Kudos to PVR for respecting the legacy of Eros while transforming it into a state-of-the-art cinema destination. If you’re in Mumbai and love movies, this place is an absolute must-visit!

featured_reviews.review_text: Eros Cinema, a landmark in Mumbai’s Churchgate area, first opened its doors in 1938, showcasing exquisite Art Deco architecture designed by Shorabji Bhedwar.  After ceasing operations in 2017, this iconic theater underwent extensive renovations and reopened in February 2024 as Eros INOX IMAX, Mumbai’s first standalone IMAX with Laser theatre.  The transformation seamlessly blends the original architectural charm with state-of-the-art cinematic technology, offering audiences an immersive viewing experience. The revamped cinema now features a 305-seat IMAX auditorium on the second floor, while preserving the historic facade and grand foyer, symbolizing a harmonious fusion of heritage and modernity.

​The biggest letdown was the audio quality. In this era of advanced surround sound and Dolby systems, this theater feels like it is stuck in the past. The bass was nonexistent, and the dialogue was barely clear.the screen quality was poor. A theater is supposed to provide an immersive experience, but this place failed on every front. I highly recommend avoiding this theater until they completely upgrade their sound system and facilities. It is a total waste of time and money.

featured_reviews.name: Alok Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Movie Time is just a 10-minute walk from the Dahisar Metro Station, but finding it was a bit of a struggle since there were no signs outside to guide us. Unlike most theatres, there’s no clear entry point, which made things confusing.

The lift situation wasn’t great either—there’s only one, and it barely fits five people, so getting in and out felt like a waiting game. Inside, there’s just one screen, and honestly, the theatre felt more like a small pod. The viewing experience was okay, but the sound quality could have been way better.

Now, let’s talk about the seats—definitely not the most comfortable. Sitting through a long movie was a bit of a task. On the plus side, the food area was clean, but the prices? Almost as high as PVR, which felt a bit much for the overall experience.

One good thing—they have free underground parking for both bikes and cars, which is a rare win in Mumbai!

Overall, if you’re nearby and just want to catch a movie, it works. But if you’re looking for a top-tier cinema experience, this might not be the best pick.

Very disappointed with the management. Every time I visit this theatre, I face the same issue regarding my bike helmet. Visitors arriving on two-wheelers are not allowed to carry helmets inside, yet there is no proper and secure facility provided to keep them. Customers are forced to leave their helmets outside at their own risk.

This is an inconvenience and a basic customer service issue that has remained unresolved despite repeated visits. If the theatre does not allow helmets inside, it should provide a safe and organized storage facility for riders.

I request the management to address this issue seriously and implement a proper solution instead of making customers face the same problem every time.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Maxus Cinemas on Gorai Road, Borivali West recently. Overall, the experience was decent, but there are a few areas that need improvement.

The biggest disappointment was that the movie started almost 30 minutes late, which was quite frustrating and affected the overall experience. The management should ensure better punctuality and timely show schedules.

The theatre is clean and the seating is comfortable. Food quality was surprisingly good, with decent options available and fresh snacks. However, the sound quality was slightly below expectations. The audio lacked depth and could definitely be improved for a better cinematic experience.

Despite these issues, the ambience is pleasant and it's still a good option for a casual movie outing with friends and family. Hoping they improve the sound system and maintain better show timings in the future.

⭐⭐⭐☆☆ (3/5)

featured_reviews.name: Dj Anu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly, really disappointed with my experience at Maxsus Cinema. The picture quality was extremely poor — the screen looked blurry, as if the sharpness wasn’t even set properly. For a premium theatre, this is just unacceptable.

On top of that, the audio was even worse. The speakers were crackling throughout, completely ruining the movie experience. Instead of immersive sound, it felt like sitting next to a broken speaker system.

Even the food was a letdown. The ₹100 sandwich was pathetic — dry, swaggy, and didn’t even have proper butter applied. Completely not worth the price.

Overall, not worth the money at all. Definitely expected much better from a brand like this.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Gandhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maxus Theatre, Borivali offers a consistently enjoyable movie-watching experience. The ambience is pleasant, seating is comfortable, and the overall layout of the theatre is well maintained, making it a great place to unwind and enjoy a film.
Audio and visual quality are impressive, with clear sound and sharp screen projection that enhance the cinematic experience. Cleanliness is well taken care of across the premises, including the seating areas and washrooms, which adds to the comfort.

Staff are courteous and helpful, and the entry and exit process is smooth without unnecessary delays. The food counter offers decent options, and service is efficient even during peak hours.

Overall, Maxus Theatre stands out as a reliable and comfortable theatre in Borivali, ideal for family outings as well as casual movie plans. Definitely a good choice for a hassle-free movie experience.

featured_reviews.name: Pankaj Powermax
featured_reviews.review_text:
INOX at Thakur Mall in Dahisar is a popular entertainment hub for residents in the Dahisar and Mira Road areas. Located on the 3rd floor of the mall, it is known for being a well-maintained multiplex that offers a premium cinematic experience at relatively competitive prices compared to other major malls in Mumbai.
Screens: The multiplex typically operates 4 screens, featuring both 2D and 3D projection technology.
​Seating: Options range from standard comfortable seating to luxury recliners (Gold Class) for a more relaxed experience.
​Audio/Visual: Equipped with high-quality sound systems, including Dolby Atmos in select halls, and large screens with high-definition picture quality.
​Accessibility: The cinema is equipped with wheelchair facilities and elevator access.
Refreshments: There is a dedicated F&B counter inside INOX serving classic movie snacks like popcorn, nachos, and sandwiches.
​Food Court: Thakur Mall itself has a multi-cuisine food court on the lower floors, offering a wider variety of dining options after the movie.
​Gaming Zone: There is a gaming area located within the mall, making it a good spot for families and children.
If you're visiting on a weekend, it's advisable to book tickets in advance via apps like BookMyShow, as it is a major landmark and can get quite crowded for blockbuster releases.
Safety system is very nice handle nicely .

featured_reviews.review_text: INOX Thakur Mall - Mira Road really impressed me! 🤩 The atmosphere was absolutely fantastic, and I had such a wonderful time. featured_reviews.name: Keval Somaiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re someone who enjoys ads more than movies, this theatre is absolutely perfect for you.

Showtime? More like “suggested time.” I’ve been here multiple times, and without fail, every single show starts 20–30 minutes late. Honestly, you could walk in 20 minutes after the scheduled time and still comfortably sit through a full ad marathon before the movie even begins.

At this point, missing a scene here is nearly impossible—not because of great service, but because punctuality clearly isn’t part of the experience.

It’s hard to tell whether the staff is just taking it easy or the management has created some magical, impossible turnaround schedule between shows. Either way, the result is the same: frustration.

A 2-hour movie somehow turns into a 3-hour commitment. Impressive… just not in the way you’d want.

Would not recommend if you value your time.

featured_reviews.name: 91 - Arsh Mansuri
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the worst theatre experiences I’ve had.

First of all, the show management was completely messed up. Instead of taking the interval at the proper time (when it was actually shown on screen), they randomly stopped the movie mid-scene after that and suddenly announced an interval 10 minutes later. It totally ruined the flow and mood of the film.

On top of that, the seats were extremely dusty and poorly maintained. Sitting there itself felt uncomfortable and unhygienic.

Overall, very disappointing experience — bad management and zero attention to cleanliness.
